summary: Stocks slipped Wednesday morning as a hot inflation reading sent Treasury yields higher, pressuring tech and chip names while the Dow held up. AAPL bucked the trend after its smart home product announcements.
market_note: Nasdaq futures down about 1% mid-morning; the VIX climbed to near 16 and the 10-year yield traded around 5.2%.

items.why: Memory and chip stocks extended declines for a third straight day after Chinese firm CXMT claimed a breakthrough in memory-chip production, weighing on the semiconductor ETF.
Goldman Sachs cut its price target to $762 from $860, flagging pressure on 2027 operating expenses from AI spending, while UBS and Guggenheim raised theirs on new AI revenue opportunities.
Shares dipped as investors digested self-driving news, including the departure of Uber's autonomous mobility president, ahead of Tesla's Roadster reveal event on October 15.
Rising after unveiling a smart home lineup including the HomeView hub and HomePod mini 2, a day after hitting an intraday record under new CEO John Ternus.
